quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'While it is true that X' concedes a fact before adding a bigger point.
quests.explanation: Concession (While it is true that automation destroys jobs) + main clause (it also creates roles nobody had imagined). 'While it is true that' balances acknowledging a fact before complicating it.
quests.textToSpeak: While it is true that automation destroys jobs, it also creates roles nobody had imagined.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The inversion 'so convinced was X' sets up the consequence of overconfidence.
quests.explanation: Degree (So convinced was the engineer of the system's fairness) + result (that she never tested its edge cases). This inverted 'so...that' shows how strong belief led to a costly oversight.
quests.textToSpeak: So convinced was the engineer of the system's fairness that she never tested its edge cases.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The cleft sentence names the deciding factor, then rules out another candidate.
quests.explanation: Cleft sentence: What ultimately tipped the balance (the focus) + was public pressure (the answer) + not scientific consensus alone (rejected alternative). 'Tip the balance' means to be the deciding factor.
quests.textToSpeak: What ultimately tipped the balance was public pressure, not scientific consensus alone.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'It takes little imagination to see X' means the conclusion is almost obvious.
quests.explanation: It takes little imagination to see (framing phrase) + why understaffed hospitals struggle with long waits (the obvious conclusion). This phrase states a cause-and-effect relationship is easy to predict.
quests.textToSpeak: It takes little imagination to see why understaffed hospitals struggle with long waits.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'However much X may Y' concedes a strong trend before contradicting it.
quests.explanation: Concession (However much streaming platforms may dominate) + main clause (live performance refuses to disappear). 'However much...may' formally grants a point before pushing back.
quests.textToSpeak: However much streaming platforms may dominate, live performance refuses to disappear.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'That X should Y is hardly surprising given Z' frames a fact as a predictable outcome.
quests.explanation: Subject clause (That wages should lag behind productivity) + judgment (is hardly surprising) + reason (given decades of policy choices). 'Should' here expresses a noteworthy fact, not obligation.
quests.textToSpeak: That wages should lag behind productivity is hardly surprising given decades of policy choices.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Not for nothing is X called Y' means the name is well-deserved.
quests.explanation: Not for nothing is encryption called (inverted clause) + the backbone of digital privacy (the label). This idiom emphasizes that a title or reputation is fully justified.
quests.textToSpeak: Not for nothing is encryption called the backbone of digital privacy.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The opening phrase generalizes a pattern; the rest gives the specific example.
quests.explanation: General pattern (As is often the case with slow disasters) + specific example (the drought drew attention only once wells ran dry). This frames one event as typical of a broader category.
quests.textToSpeak: As is often the case with slow disasters, the drought drew attention only once wells ran dry.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'It matters little how X if Y' dismisses one factor in favor of a more decisive one.
quests.explanation: Dismissed factor (It matters little how advanced the treatment is) + decisive condition (if patients cannot afford it). This structure shifts focus to what truly determines the outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: It matters little how advanced the treatment is if patients cannot afford it.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Two advanced pieces combine here: a concession, plus a relative clause at the end.
quests.explanation: Concession (While it is true that translation loses nuance) + main clause (it still opens doors) + that silence never could (relative clause). The relative clause modifies 'doors', adding a final contrast.
quests.textToSpeak: While it is true that translation loses nuance, it still opens doors that silence never could.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'So dependent had X become that Y' is an inverted past perfect 'so...that' structure.
quests.explanation: Degree (So dependent had the region become on a single export) + result (that one bad season crippled it). Past perfect ('had become') shows the dependency built up before the crisis hit.
quests.textToSpeak: So dependent had the region become on a single export that one bad season crippled it.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The cleft sentence names the true goal, distinguishing it from an assumed one.
quests.explanation: Cleft sentence: What the algorithm optimized for (the focus) + was engagement (the real goal) + not necessarily the user's wellbeing (rejected assumption). 'Optimize for' means to design toward a specific outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: What the algorithm optimized for was engagement, not necessarily the user's wellbeing.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'However carefully X was managed' concedes strong effort before naming a persistent threat.
quests.explanation: Concession (However carefully the reserve was managed) + main clause (poaching still threatened the last remaining herds). Even careful management couldn't fully solve the problem.
quests.textToSpeak: However carefully the reserve was managed, poaching still threatened the last remaining herds.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'That X is a Y worth Z' turns a whole fact into the sentence's subject.
quests.explanation: Subject clause (That the vaccine reached remote villages at all) + judgment (is a logistical achievement worth celebrating). 'At all' emphasizes how difficult the achievement was.
quests.textToSpeak: That the vaccine reached remote villages at all is a logistical achievement worth celebrating.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Not for nothing do X' emphasizes that survival wasn't accidental.
quests.explanation: Not for nothing do festivals like this survive (inverted clause) + centuries of political upheaval (the challenge survived). This idiom implies deep cultural resilience explains the survival.
quests.textToSpeak: Not for nothing do festivals like this survive centuries of political upheaval.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: A general pattern (opening) frames a specific, familiar story (the rest).
quests.explanation: General pattern (As is often the case with new technology) + specific example (regulation arrived only after the damage was done). Implies the example is part of a recurring pattern.
quests.textToSpeak: As is often the case with new technology, regulation arrived only after the damage was done.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The obvious cause-and-effect chain is framed as easy to picture.
quests.explanation: It takes little imagination to see (framing phrase) + how tariffs ripple through an entire supply chain (the obvious effect). 'Ripple through' is a vivid metaphor for a spreading, indirect effect.
quests.textToSpeak: It takes little imagination to see how tariffs ripple through an entire supply chain.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The inversion sets up a dramatic, formally stated consequence.
quests.explanation: Degree (So severe had the coral bleaching become) + result (that entire reef systems were declared functionally dead). 'Functionally dead' precisely describes a severely damaged ecosystem.
quests.textToSpeak: So severe had the coral bleaching become that entire reef systems were declared functionally dead.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: This shortened concession drops 'is' or 'was' for a punchier rhythm.
quests.explanation: Concession (However well-funded the research) + main clause (some diseases resist every treatment tried so far). Dropping the verb after the adjective is a common shortcut in formal writing.
quests.textToSpeak: However well-funded the research, some diseases resist every treatment tried so far.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The cleft sentence draws a subtle distinction between two related ideas.
quests.explanation: Cleft sentence: What the festival ultimately preserved (the focus) + was not tradition itself (rejected answer) + but the memory of belonging (real answer). Distinguishes a concrete idea from an emotional one.
quests.textToSpeak: What the festival ultimately preserved was not tradition itself, but the memory of belonging.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'That X is easy to forget' points out an overlooked truth.
quests.explanation: Subject clause (That small businesses absorbed most of the shock) + judgment (is easy to forget in hindsight). Often precedes a call to remember an underappreciated group.
quests.textToSpeak: That small businesses absorbed most of the shock is easy to forget in hindsight.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The passive verb 'are required' fits naturally into this inverted idiom.
quests.explanation: Not for nothing are engineers now required (inverted clause, passive) + to document every automated decision (the requirement). Implies the new rule exists for a well-justified reason.
quests.textToSpeak: Not for nothing are engineers now required to document every automated decision.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Again, a general pattern frames a specific lesson learned.
quests.explanation: General pattern (As is often the case with restoration projects) + specific lesson (patience mattered more than funding). Lends broader credibility to a single project's experience.
quests.textToSpeak: As is often the case with restoration projects, patience mattered more than funding.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: A promise is dismissed in favor of a more reliable, concrete source of truth.
quests.explanation: Dismissed factor (It matters little what the label promises) + decisive condition (if the ingredients tell a different story). This pattern favors evidence over marketing claims.
quests.textToSpeak: It matters little what the label promises if the ingredients tell a different story.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The inversion shows how deeply embedded a practice had become.
quests.explanation: Degree (So central had oral storytelling become) + result (that written records were considered almost unnecessary). Past perfect shows this importance built up over a long period.
quests.textToSpeak: So central had oral storytelling become that written records were considered almost unnecessary.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: One virtue is granted; a second, less-rewarded virtue is introduced.
quests.explanation: Concession (While it is true that markets reward efficiency) + main clause (they rarely reward patience). Useful for pointing out what a system fails to value.
quests.textToSpeak: While it is true that markets reward efficiency, they rarely reward patience.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The cleft sentence sets up a surprising, almost humorous contrast.
quests.explanation: Cleft sentence: What ultimately exposed the flaw (the focus) + was not an audit (expected answer, rejected) + but a curious teenager (the real, surprising answer). Works well for an unexpected twist.
quests.textToSpeak: What ultimately exposed the flaw was not an audit, but a curious teenager.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Another shortened concession: 'However remote the island' implies 'is'.
quests.explanation: Concession (However remote the island) + main clause (plastic waste still finds its way to its shores). Even extreme distance doesn't fully protect against a global problem.
quests.textToSpeak: However remote the island, plastic waste still finds its way to its shores.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'That X is precisely why Y' links one surprising fact directly to its cause.
quests.explanation: Subject clause (That the treatment costs so little) + judgment (is precisely why it was never marketed aggressively). Implies a slightly cynical, but logical, explanation.
quests.textToSpeak: That the treatment costs so little is precisely why it was never marketed aggressively.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Present perfect fits naturally into this inverted idiom, showing accumulated achievement.
quests.explanation: Not for nothing has this novel been translated (inverted present perfect, passive) + into more languages than any other this century (the achievement). Implies the novel's wide reach is well-earned.
quests.textToSpeak: Not for nothing has this novel been translated into more languages than any other this century.
